messages.author: 75b52a97a8fa5e5f
messages.subject: RmaPlm
parts:
Hi,

I got memory error as below in using RmaPlm. (windows XP 4G memory in
the machine).

> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("anth", chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")
> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2");
> setCdf(cs, cdf);
> plm <- RmaPlm(cs)
> fit(plm)
Loading required package: preprocessCore
Error in fitfcn(y) : Calloc could not allocate (27206656 of 8) memory
>
how can I solve the problem?

thanks
Yuan

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] RmaPlm
parts:
Yuan.

Just like on the Bioconductor list, you will get more help (and quicker!)
on these lists if you read the posting guide and give people more
description of what you are actually doing. It also helps if you try some
debugging yourself and/or searching the mailing lists for other's past
problems. For example, a 'sessionInfo()' so we know what packages you
have loaded, etc. Perhaps a 'traceback()' to see where the error occured.

In addition to those, can you give us the output of 'print(cdf)' and
'print(cs)'.

Also, you might set up verbose output so you can see how far the routine
made it:

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)

...

fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

What CDF file are you using?

Cheers,
Mark

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] RmaPlm
parts:
Hi Yuan,
It looks like, based on your code, that you are using the cdf
distributed by Affymetrix. ('fromChipType' command will pull this one.)
This cdf has a number of EXTREMELY large probesets that consist of
control probes -- see previous discussions on this. I don't know that
others actually run out of memory using this cdf previously -- other
reports are just that it takes days, but I think they had quite large
machines--but that's likely the culprit.

The better solution -- even if you just want summaries per probesets
(exon) -- is to use the ExonRmaPlm function and choose mergeGroups=F AND
use one of the cdfs that we have distributed on the group pages that
group the probesets by transcript cluster (for example) and which also
get rid of these probes as a side product (e.g.
HuEx-1_0-st-v2,mainRx,A2007xxxx,EP.cdf, which includes all 'main' design
probesets). See the example code for an exon array analysis on the group
pages to see how to change your cdf and use ExonRmaPlm.
Best,
Elizabeth

What Elizabeth is saying is that you should *not* use the CDF file
named HuEx-1_0-st-v2.cdf, which is the one that originates from
Affymetrix (ASCII or binary). It contains a few units that contains
units with extremely large number of probes. You do not want to use
that CDF! Instead you want to use one of the custom CDF provided by
Elizabeth and available on the group web page. See refers you to:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/affymetrix-defined-transcript-clusters

/Henrik
